questions.question: Have you experienced an unexplained loss of appetite recently?

effects.safety: Context only. An unexplained persistent loss of appetite can warrant appropriate medical attention; the quiz should not infer a cause.
effects.report: Normally no headline score. May be flagged as a contextual symptom if relevant to other responses.

questions.question: How much caffeine do you typically consume on a normal day?

effects.safety: Do not treat caffeine quantity alone as evidence of poor health.
effects.report: Provides a caffeine-exposure context that can be interpreted with sleep quality, daytime sleepiness and caffeine timing.

questions.question: How late in the day do you usually have your last caffeinated drink?
options: I do not have caffeinated drinks

effects.safety: Do not treat timing alone as evidence of a sleep disorder.
effects.report: Can strengthen a Sleep & Recovery interpretation when later caffeine is combined with poor sleep or daytime sleepiness.

questions.question: How often do you feel irritable, impatient or easily frustrated?

effects.report: Higher frequency contributes to Mood, Stress & Emotional Balance.

questions.question: Do you have any food, chemical or environmental sensitivities or intolerances that we should take into account?

effects.safety: Recommendation filter. Sensitivity/intolerance should not be presented as an allergy or diagnosis.
effects.report: Used primarily to personalise recommendations and contextualise relevant responses.

questions.logic: None is mutually exclusive with all other choices.

questions.question: Have you experienced recurring yeast or fungal problems that you are concerned about?

effects.safety: Medical context only. Do not score as evidence of poor immune function, gut health or microbiome imbalance.
effects.report: Normally no headline report effect; may be retained for contextual/recommendation handling.

design_note: Q37 is now quantity only, with Q37b separately capturing timing. Q36, Q39 and Q40 are context/safety questions rather than outcome scores. Q38 is a direct mood/stress signal.
